content: Root cause: The bug was caused by the USB-DMAC driver incorrectly handling interrupts when the CHCR.DE (DMA Enable) bit was not set. The driver was calling the `usb_dmac_isr_transfer_end()` function even when the DE bit was 0, which could lead to a NULL descriptor being passed to that function. This situation arose because the driver did not properly check the state of the CHCR.DE bit before processing the transfer end, resulting in potential dereferencing of a NULL pointer. The patch fixes this by ensuring that `usb_dmac_isr_transfer_end()` is only called when the DE bit is set to 1.
